name: 舎鈴 新宿センタービル店 (Sharin — Shinjuku Center Building)

claims.text: Sharin's chain-wide allergen notice states that individual sensitivity to allergens varies, that it cannot guarantee a customer won't react, that ingredients can pick up trace allergens during sourcing or in-kitchen prep, that secondary cross-contamination cannot be fully prevented, and that cooking tools and tableware are not dedicated per dish.

A chain-wide printable allergen list (covering items such as shrimp, crab, walnut, wheat, buckwheat, egg, dairy, peanut and more) is published by the brand for customers to check ingredients themselves; there is no branch-specific note about staff proactively managing allergy requests.

name: 渋谷 ガパオ食堂 (Shibuya Gapao Shokudo (Gapao Shokudo Shibuya)

claims.text: Signature dishes such as Gapao Rice are prepared with oyster sauce and fish sauce as base seasonings; oyster sauce and any soy sauce used typically contain wheat, and this has not been confirmed as gluten-free at this restaurant.
A restaurant listing states customers with allergies are welcome to contact the restaurant, implying staff will field allergy questions on request, though no formal allergen menu was found.

name: 渋谷カオマンガイ (Shibuya Khao Man Gai)

claims.text: The special dipping sauce is a fermented blend of Thai miso, soy sauce, and black vinegar soy sauce; soy sauce used in Japan typically contains wheat unless a store specifies otherwise, which was not found for this shop.
Noodles are two-eight (nihachi) soba — roughly 80% buckwheat, 20% wheat flour — so the noodle itself contains gluten; standard soba tsuyu also relies on wheat-based shoyu.

Vegetables are pesticide-free and delivered fresh each morning from a contracted farm on the Miura Peninsula, and fish is sourced fresh daily from Sukumo Port in Kochi — a whole-ingredient, made-to-order kitchen rather than a processed-food operation, though this is not a documented allergy protocol.

All kushi-age skewers — meat, seafood, and vegetable alike — are coated with the restaurant's original panko breadcrumb and fried in the same oil at the open counter, so there is no separate gluten-free preparation.
Vegetable skewers are fried in the same shared oil, at the same counter, as the meat and seafood skewers.
Roughly 40 of the restaurant's approximately 150 skewer ingredients are vegetables (e.g. asparagus, garlic), a wider vegetable selection than at most kushi-age shops.

name: そば処 信州屋 新宿南口店 (Shinshuya Shinjuku Minamiguchi-ten (Soba-dok)

claims.text: Tempura and soba are made fresh to order in-house (stone-ground soba flour, extrusion noodle-making, boiled to order) rather than pre-made, per the operator's own description of its process.

name: 精進ラーメン菜 (Shojin Ramen Sai)

claims.text: Instagram visitor caption: "Vegetarian heaven in the heart of Shibuya! 🌱✨" describing it as a rare fully meat-free spot in the area.
